reason: The membrane fats are the clearest starting point for building a boundary around the water.
expectation: The fats and water will form the basis of an enclosed cell.

alternatives.reason: Checking their available partners could clarify how to build the boundary.

effect: The fats formed a closed boundary around water, but it still lacks protein channels needed for a selective boundary.
reaction: The picture makes the missing channels clear.
reason: The transport proteins have channels that could make the enclosure selective.
expectation: The transport proteins will fit into the boundary and allow selected substances to cross.

effect: The enclosure now has protein channels, and the picture shows charged particles still outside.
reaction: The remaining particles suggest a clear next step.
reason: Mineral salts supply the charged particles shown outside the selective boundary.
expectation: The salts will enter the enclosure to form cell fluid.

effect: The salts completed the muscle-cell model's selective boundary, revealing slots for stored instructions and ATP machinery.
reaction: The new slots make the next stage clear.
reason: DNA stores instructions, and the nuclear envelopes appear to provide a place to hold it.
expectation: The DNA will be enclosed to make stored instructions for the cell.

effect: The DNA and nuclear envelopes made muscle nuclei, which appear to fill the stored instructions slot.
reaction: The porous membranes connect the nuclei to the earlier picture of instructions leaving through pores.
reason: The muscle nuclei contain the stored instructions needed by the cell model.
expectation: The nuclei will fit into the stored instructions slot.

effect: The nuclei filled the stored instructions slot; the ATP machinery is still needed.
reaction: The inset reinforces how copied instructions leave the nuclei.
reason: Mitochondria are the available structures associated with oxygen-using ATP production.
expectation: The mitochondria will fill the oxygen-using ATP machinery slot.

effect: The mitochondria filled the ATP machinery slot, and the new goal is to make and install pulling structures.
reaction: The fuel, oxygen and ATP diagram makes the mitochondria's role clearer.
reason: The introduction says to use copied instructions to make the pulling proteins, and ribosomes are shown producing a protein chain from a coded strip.
expectation: The ribosomes will use the copied instructions to make pulling proteins.

effect: The copied instructions and ribosomes produced pulling protein threads while both remained available, so the threads appear ready to add to the cell model.
reaction: The two panels make the connection between protein production and organized filaments clear.
reason: The cell model needs pulling structures, and the new threads appear to provide them.
expectation: The threads will fit into the muscle-cell model as its pulling structures.

effect: Adding the pulling protein threads transformed the cell model into muscle fibers and completed the chapter. The final picture shows how greater filament overlap shortens the repeating units without shortening the filaments themselves.
reaction: The two poses made the pulling mechanism more interesting and concrete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the pulling threads was most worthwhile because the resulting picture connected protein structures inside cells to muscle shortening.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding mineral salts was the least clear step: the charged particles suggested what to do, but the result did not explain much about their role in cell fluid.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the filaments keep their length while their increased overlap shortens the repeating unit.

arbitrary.text: The mineral salts combination felt somewhat underexplained; the picture suggested the match, but not why those salts were needed to complete the model.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the muscle fibers are organized into tissues and connected to other body systems.
